title: Orientation datum
statement:
Work in the six-functor datum [def-sf-datum], with finite-type schemes over the fixed algebraic closure $k$ of a finite field of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and the coefficient stages $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$. Use its bounded constructible finite-Tor categories, adjunctions, exchange and projection transformations, and coefficient comparisons. The coefficient objects $\Lambda_T$, Tate twists and shifts are those of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] and [def-sf-datum]: $K(m)=K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_T}\Lambda_T(m)$; the integral unit and tensor products are completed, and the algebraically closed field stage is interpreted at a common finite coefficient extension.

An *orientation datum* is a family, for every smooth separated finite-type $k$-morphism $f:X\to Y$ of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and every displayed coefficient stage, of isomorphisms
$$
\gamma_{f,\Lambda_Y}:Lf^*\Lambda_Y(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf^!\Lambda_Y
$$
in $D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$, subject to the compatibility and normalization conditions below. At finite coefficients $A=A_{E,n}$ the family also includes the etale components: for every such $f$, an isomorphism $\gamma^{e}_{f}:f_e^{*}L_Y(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}f^{\times}A_Y$ in $D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, where $f^{\times}$ is the etale right adjoint of etale compact support from which $Rf^!$ is transported in [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], and $L_T(d)$ is the ordinary etale twist of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] built from $L_T=\mu^{\mathrm{et}}_{\ell^r,T}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell^r}A_T$ for some $r\geq1$ with $\ell^rA=0$ (the canonical identifications for different $r$ in that node are understood). The realization equation in clause 3 relates $\gamma^e_f$ to the pro-etale component $\gamma_{f,A_Y}$. Put $T_{X,d}=\Lambda_X(d)[2d]$ and $\omega_f=Rf^!\Lambda_Y$, and use the coefficient-unit identification to write the component also as $\gamma_f:T_{X,d}\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_f$.

Here are the precise comparison conventions, all formed from the supplied datum. Write $\varepsilon_f:Rf_!Rf^!\to\mathrm{id}$ for the counit. For $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$, let
$$
\theta_{f,K}:Lf^*K\otimes^L\omega_f\longrightarrow Rf^!K
$$
be the adjoint transpose of
$$
Rf_!(Lf^*K\otimes^L\omega_f)\cong Rf_!(\omega_f\otimes^LLf^*K)
\xrightarrow{\operatorname{PF}^{-1}}Rf_!\omega_f\otimes^LK
\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_{f,\Lambda_Y}\otimes1}\Lambda_Y\otimes^LK\cong K.
$$
For a Cartesian square in this setting
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X'&\xrightarrow{u}&X\\
f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
Y'&\xrightarrow{v}&Y,
\end{array}
$$
let $\beta_{f,v}:Lu^*\omega_f\to\omega_{f'}$ be the adjoint transpose under $Rf'_!\dashv Rf'^!$ of
$$
Rf'_!Lu^*\omega_f\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Ex}_!^{-1}}Lv^*Rf_!\omega_f
\xrightarrow{Lv^*\varepsilon_{f,\Lambda_Y}}Lv^*\Lambda_Y\cong\Lambda_{Y'}.
$$
The inverse projection and exchange maps used here are part of axioms (A3) and (A2) of [def-sf-datum]. These formulas specify maps; no assertion of smooth purity is built into their definition.

1. **Naturality in the base, including etale base change.** In every such square, with $f$ smooth of pure relative dimension $d$, require
$$
\gamma_{f'}=\beta_{f,v}\circ Lu^*(\gamma_f)\circ\bigl(T_{X',d}\xrightarrow{\sim}Lu^*T_{X,d}\bigr).
$$
The last identification is the pullback, twist and shift comparison. In particular impose this equation when $v$ is etale. The squares range over the fixed finite-type setting: $Y'$ is a finite-type $k$-scheme and $v$ is a separated finite-type morphism, the domain on which (A2) supplies $\operatorname{Ex}_!$; no properness or smoothness of $v$ is added.

2. **Composition.** For smooth separated finite-type $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to Z$ of pure relative dimensions $d$ and $e$, require $\gamma_{g\circ f}$ to be the composite
$$
\begin{aligned}
T_{X,d+e}&\cong Lf^*T_{Y,e}\otimes^LT_{X,d}
\xrightarrow{1\otimes\gamma_f}Lf^*T_{Y,e}\otimes^L\omega_f
\xrightarrow{\theta_{f,T_{Y,e}}}Rf^!T_{Y,e}\\
&\xrightarrow{Rf^!(\gamma_g)}Rf^!Rg^!\Lambda_Z
\xrightarrow{\sim}R(g\circ f)^!\Lambda_Z.
\end{aligned}
$$
The first isomorphism is twist multiplicativity and tensor-shift compatibility; the last is the right-adjoint composition comparison corresponding to (A1) and (A4) of [def-sf-datum].

3. **Coefficient comparisons and pro-etale realization.** For each comparison functor $C_T$ supplied by (A5), let $t_C:C_XT_{X,d}\xrightarrow{\sim}T'_{X,d}$ and $w_C:C_X\omega_f\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega'_f$ be its twist and exceptional-image comparisons. Require the equality of maps from $C_XT_{X,d}$ to $\omega'_f$
$$
w_C\circ C_X(\gamma_f)=\gamma'_f\circ t_C.
$$
This is required for finite reductions $A_{E,n}\to A_{E,m}$ ($1\leq m\leq n$), integral-to-finite reductions, scalar extension and rationalization, and common-stage finite coefficient extensions, exactly on the domains specified by (A5). The same equation expresses compatibility with the pro-etale realization: at finite coefficients $C_T=\nu_T^*$ is the derived etale-to-pro-etale pullback [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback], the unprimed component is the etale component $\gamma^e_f$, and the primed orientation is the pro-etale one $\gamma_{f,A_Y}$. Here $t_C:\nu_X^*\bigl(L_X(d)[2d]\bigr)\xrightarrow{\sim}A_X(d)[2d]$ is the $d$-th tensor power, shifted, of the comparison $\tau_X:\nu_X^*L_X\xrightarrow{\sim}A_X(1)$ of [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison] (applied over the base $X$), and $w_C:\nu_X^*f^{\times}A_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}\nu_X^*f^{\times}R\nu_{Y,*}\nu_Y^*A_Y=Rf^!A_Y$ is induced by the unit $A_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}R\nu_{Y,*}\nu_Y^*A_Y$, as in [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. At integral and field stages use the completed, rationalized and common-stage comparisons of the datum. No reduction from field coefficients to finite coefficients is meant.

4. **Affine-line normalization.** For the projection $\pi:\mathbf A^1_Y\to Y$, require $\gamma_{\pi,\Lambda_Y}$ to equal its canonical affine-line orientation. Explicitly at finite coefficients $A=A_{E,n}$, take the standard compactification $\mathbf A^1_Y\xrightarrow{j}\mathbf P^1_Y\xrightarrow{q}Y$. Choose $r\geq1$ with $\ell^r A=0$ and let $B_T=\mu^{\mathrm{et}}_{\ell^r,T}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell^r}A_T$ on the etale site. Let $t_q^e:Rq_{e,*}B_{\mathbf P^1_Y}[2]\to A_Y$ be the trace of [def-amb-p1-trace] at $N=\ell^r$. With $C_T=\nu_T^*$, use the twist comparison $\tau_T:C_TB_T\xrightarrow{\sim}A_T(1)$ and the proper direct-image comparison $\beta_q:C_YRq_{e,*}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rq_{p,*}C_{\mathbf P^1_Y}$ of [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison]. Here the subscripts $e,p$ distinguish the etale and pro-etale operations. On the twist-identified source define
$$
t_q^p=C_Y(t_q^e)\circ\bigl(Rq_{p,*}(\tau_{\mathbf P^1_Y}[2])\circ\beta_{q,B_{\mathbf P^1_Y}[2]}\bigr)^{-1}:
Rq_{p,*}A_{\mathbf P^1_Y}(1)[2]\longrightarrow A_Y.
$$
The cited comparison statement also identifies the open-extension counits and makes this trace independent of $r$. In the following pro-etale formula write $t_q=t_q^p$ and suppress the site subscripts. Define
$$
\int_\pi:R\pi_!A_{\mathbf A^1_Y}(1)[2]=Rq_*j_!A_{\mathbf A^1_Y}(1)[2]
\xrightarrow{Rq_*(\varepsilon^j)}Rq_*A_{\mathbf P^1_Y}(1)[2]\xrightarrow{t_q}A_Y,
$$
where $\varepsilon^j:j_!j^*\to\mathrm{id}$ is the extension-by-zero counit. The canonical orientation is the adjoint transpose under $R\pi_!\dashv R\pi^!$ of $\int_\pi$. Impose equality with this map, with the pullback-unit identification on its source. At integral coefficients the canonical normalization has these finite reductions; at rational and algebraically closed coefficients it is their rationalization and common-stage scalar extension. These are the coefficient conventions of [def-sf-datum].

The conditions are on the entire family, including its coefficient and realization components. Existence of a family satisfying them is a separate theorem, not an assertion of this definition. For $f=a_X:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, when $X$ is smooth separated of pure dimension $d$, the component read in reverse is exactly $\omega_{X,\Lambda}\cong\Lambda_X(d)[2d]$, with $\omega_{X,\Lambda}=Ra_X^!\Lambda$ as in [def-sf-datum].

split_report.summary: One-level definition split with no new nodes: retained every family, naturality, composition, coefficient, realization and affine-line-normalization clause. Named the existing coefficient/twist, smooth-dimension, realization and projective-line-trace notions. Wrote the comparison maps and the required equations using only the six-functor datum, including an explicit affine-line normalization valid for a nonseparated finite-type base. No existence or invertibility theorem has been inserted into the definition. The finite-coefficient project record is not an exact attachment for the full coefficient family. Second reading made the finite etale companion components explicit and specified the finite trace realization, including the roots-of-unity twist comparison, by an existing comparison statement. Maintainer reader fix: named the etale components by the etale exceptional adjoint of def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image and the etale twist of lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback, wrote the realization comparisons t_C and w_C explicitly, and made explicit that the base-change squares use separated finite-type v as in (A2).
split_report.blueprint: Realizes every clause of current main-20261015 def-sf-orientation (order 2391) and the orientation interface of sk-def-sf-orientation: component isomorphism, naturality, composition, etale base change, finite reduction, scalar extension, pro-etale realization, affine-line normalization, and structure-morphism reading. This definition has no proof steps. The unit already has its own separate key node sk-def-sf-orientation, so no unit realization field is edited.
